title: What if robots didn't need all their AI onboard?
gist: Microsoft Research argues that robots should not run physical AI inference only on onboard GPUs. In its measurements, offloading inference to edge or cloud GPUs raised task success and extended battery life. Microsoft has added a Kubernetes-based offload capability to its open-source Physical AI Toolchain, which integrates Azure with NVIDIA's physical AI stack.

insights.claim: The prevailing robotics design puts a GPU onboard the robot and runs task-execution inference there, sending only higher-level planning to the cloud. Microsoft Research explicitly challenges this assumption.
insights.speaker: Brenda Potts
insights.so_what: If robot inference moves off the device, demand for robot compute shifts from embedded GPUs toward edge and cloud GPU capacity, which matters for robot BOM costs and for data-center demand.
insights.quote: While higher-level planning may be performed in the cloud, task execution typically remains tied to the robot itself. We challenge this assumption.
insights.locator: Today, the prevailing approach to physical AI

insights.claim: Onboard GPUs draw significant power, shorten battery life, add cost and weight, and can prevent robots from running the latest generation of AI models. These constraints grow as physical AI models get larger.
insights.speaker: Brenda Potts
insights.so_what: As models scale, onboard robot compute runs into a structural ceiling, which strengthens the case for a remote-inference architecture.
insights.quote: GPUs consume significant power, reduce battery life, add cost and weight, and can limit the ability to run the latest generation of AI models.
insights.locator: Today, the prevailing approach to physical AI

insights.claim: Microsoft Research frames physical AI progress along three dimensions: robot hardware, embodied AI models, and systems infrastructure for training and inference. It singles out inference infrastructure as the under-addressed bottleneck, since hardware and models have advanced rapidly.
insights.speaker: Brenda Potts
insights.so_what: Inference orchestration for robots is flagged as an under-served layer, so watch for infrastructure and tooling plays rather than only hardware or model makers.
insights.quote: we turn our focus on a relatively under-addressed aspect: inference infrastructure of physical AI

insights.claim: Microsoft Research describes its work as the first systematic study of robotics workloads. It covers mobile manipulation (for example, finding rubbish in a kitchen and throwing it away) across semantic mapping and planning, navigation, and manipulation models, run on onboard, edge, and cloud compute configurations.
insights.speaker: Brenda Potts
insights.so_what: The study sets a benchmark framing for deciding where to place robot compute that vendors and integrators are likely to cite.
insights.locator: To better understand the systems implications of physical AI

insights.claim: Some smaller GPUs could not fit the mobile manipulation stack in memory at all. On GPUs with enough memory, mapping and planning ran up to 383% slower than on an NVIDIA A100, which limits the robot's ability to operate in dynamic spaces.
insights.speaker: Brenda Potts
insights.so_what: GPU memory and throughput limit what an embedded robot can run, which favors data-center-class GPUs for robot inference.
insights.quote: On GPUs with sufficient memory, mapping and planning slowed by up to 383% compared to an A100

insights.claim: With lighter GPUs, robot navigation detected obstacles on time 30% less often.
insights.speaker: Brenda Potts
insights.so_what: Underpowered onboard compute has a safety cost, not just a speed cost, which matters for deploying robots around people.
insights.quote: Navigation showed a 30% drop in its timely detection of obstacles with lighter GPUs.

insights.claim: Vision-language-action (VLA) models slowed only modestly on smaller GPUs, but that small slowdown was enough to cut their accuracy by 50%. Even minor latency penalties can degrade robot manipulation severely.
insights.speaker: Brenda Potts
insights.so_what: Robot manipulation accuracy is very sensitive to latency, so inference speed is a make-or-break spec for VLA deployments.
insights.quote: While the VLA models did not dramatically slow down with smaller GPUs, the slowdown was still sufficient to drop their accuracies by 50%.

insights.claim: In the study, success rates for robot arms handing objects to each other went up when inference was offloaded from onboard GPUs to on-premise or cloud GPUs.
insights.speaker: Brenda Potts
insights.so_what: The study gives direct evidence that remote inference can make robots more capable, not only cheaper.
insights.locator: Figure 4: Success rates of robot arms handing over objects

insights.claim: Microsoft Research predicts that the benefits of offloading robot inference will grow as physical AI models keep increasing in size and complexity.
insights.speaker: Brenda Potts
insights.so_what: If model scaling continues, edge and cloud GPU demand from robotics should grow faster than demand for onboard robot compute.
insights.quote: As physical AI models continue to grow in size and complexity, the benefits of offloading are likely to become even more pronounced.

insights.claim: Microsoft Research replaced a robot's onboard GPU with a Raspberry Pi-5 board that sends all data to an offloaded GPU. The study found that large onboard GPUs such as NVIDIA's Jetson Thor drained robot batteries by up to 160% (a few hours of runtime), measured on the Stretch-3 robot.
insights.speaker: Brenda Potts
insights.so_what: Swapping premium embedded GPUs for cheap boards plus remote inference could lengthen robot uptime and cut unit cost, a potential headwind for high-end embedded robot compute.
insights.quote: The larger onboard GPUs, such as Jetson Thor, drained robot batteries by up to 160% (or a few hours) for even the larger robots.

insights.claim: Offloading robot inference involves a complex tradeoff between performance, network latency and bandwidth, and available GPU resources. It is not a free win, and the result depends on connectivity and on the remote compute available.
insights.speaker: Brenda Potts
insights.so_what: Offloaded robotics depends on low-latency on-premise and edge networking, which is a potential demand driver for private 5G and edge data centers.
insights.quote: offloading inference out of the robot involves a complex tradeoff involving performance, network latency and bandwidth, and available GPU resources

insights.claim: Microsoft has built a Kubernetes-based toolset that automatically containerizes robotics AI workloads from declarative specifications. It distributes those workloads across the robot, edge GPUs, and cloud overflow using placement policies, and it integrates with robotic simulators, LeRobot, and ROS2.
insights.speaker: Brenda Potts
insights.so_what: Microsoft is positioning cloud-native orchestration as the control plane for robot fleets, which could pull robotics inference spend onto Azure.
insights.quote: Kubernetes is a natural platform to provide a uniform abstraction to distribute robotic AI between the robot’s compute, edge GPU, and overflowing to the cloud.

insights.claim: Microsoft's Physical AI Toolchain is an open-source, production-ready framework that integrates Microsoft Azure cloud services with NVIDIA's physical AI stack. It automates data curation, augmentation, and evaluation across perception, mobility, imitation learning, and reinforcement learning pipelines.
insights.speaker: Brenda Potts
insights.so_what: The Microsoft-NVIDIA alignment in physical AI tooling strengthens Azure as a home for robotics workloads and adds another demand channel for NVIDIA.
insights.locator: Microsoft has recently released the Physical AI Toolchain

insights.claim: Microsoft calls its offloaded physical AI inference capability in the Physical AI Toolchain industry-first. The release ships example projects for the SO-101 and UR10e robot arms and demonstrates Microsoft's dual-arm Rho model offloaded to a Jetson Thor GPU that controls a Mobile Aloha robot.
insights.speaker: Brenda Potts
insights.so_what: Microsoft has its own robot foundation model (Rho) plus deployment tooling, so it is building a full-stack physical AI position worth tracking against other robotics platform efforts.
insights.quote: We are announcing the addition of an industry-first capability for offloaded physical AI inference for robots as part of the Physical AI Toolchain.
insights.locator: Microsoft has recently released the Physical AI Toolchain
